customChangeSurface.description: DS Harness product flavor, bundle identity, startup shell, single-instance ownership, and official-product isolation.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Electron product configuration, environment-resolved app id, userData resolution, single-instance ownership, mandatory-update identity, and the startup web document contract.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: A regression can rename the product, reuse the official profile/userData boundary, or show stale official branding.

customChangeSurface.description: Desktop staging, primary-runtime closure, Electron packaging, and the qualified install artifact contract.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Desktop staging layout, primary-runtime descriptor and payload digests, packaged Node/Python/pnpm tree, package resolution, and release-family build contracts.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Changes can produce an incomplete runtime, wrong architecture, missing native module, unqualified update payload, or non-replayable product build.

customChangeSurface.description: The `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-custom` Cordis tail patch that layers the DS Harness capability composition onto the upstream base/web bundles. The historical `desktop-custom-composition` / `desktop-dev-composition` package-set implementation is retired and is not restored.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Cordis patch schema, base/web bundle graph, package export resolution, generated catalogs, and Desktop package-set loading.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Composition drift can silently omit a capability, add an unused runtime row, or make the Custom runtime fail during startup.

customChangeSurface.description: The Stage 6-11 DS Harness capability packages layered over upstream agent, session, LLM, compaction, and client contracts.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Agent lifecycle events, LLM streaming/retry hooks, Session v3 events/projections, compaction executor, token-meter, Typert Remote streams, Gateway transport, Resource Registry, and scoped client slots.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Interface drift can break observability, task continuity, or safety invariants while leaving the Desktop superficially runnable.

customChangeSurface.description: Desktop flavor, profile resolution, and the intentional isolation/sharing boundary for userData, settings, sessions, and migration.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Profile link/loading, project and runtime descriptors, userData, settings, sessions, and automatic migration semantics.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: This is a data-safety boundary; a mismatch can mix official and Custom runtime state or migrate shared data unexpectedly.

customChangeSurface.description: Run Details, the transient diagnostics dock, and the client composition that mounts them.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Client remote transport, generated client catalogs, dockkit and scoped slots, conversation layout, startup URL, and title/branding contracts.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Changes can hide diagnostics, reintroduce an idle dock gap, or surface official branding.

customChangeSurface.description: Contract, composition, packaging, UI, and maintenance-tooling regressions.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Vitest, test helpers, Desktop fixtures, and package build conventions.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Test-framework drift can hide or falsely report compatibility failures; it does not itself prove a product regression.

customChangeSurface.description: Bilingual architecture notes, subsystem pages, generated catalogs, and maintenance evidence.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Documentation pairing, generated-catalog, link, and architecture-note conventions.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Documentation drift is normally non-runtime but can invalidate generated-doc gates and maintenance evidence.

customChangeSurface.description: Workspace discovery, TypeScript project references, package exports, and build/release tooling.
customChangeSurface.upstreamDependency: Workspace discovery, TypeScript project references, package exports, build/release tooling, and dependency resolution.
customChangeSurface.riskSignificance: Structural drift can make Custom packages disappear from builds or resolve incompatible runtime dependencies.

seams.description: Product flavor, bundle identity, startup shell, userData, and single-instance isolation for DS Harness.
seams.interface: Electron productFlavor/appId identity, app.setPath('userData'), single-instance ownership, startup document/title, and flavor selection.
seams.whyItMatters: The product identity and the official/Custom data boundary are the first safety gate of any candidate launch.
seams.failureMode: A regression renames the product, reuses the official profile or userData, or lets both applications contend for one identity.
seams.detectionMethod: Exact path and rename detection; product/data-safety contract paths are treated as structural signals.

seams.description: Desktop staging, primary-runtime closure, Electron packaging, and Custom install artifact contract.
seams.interface: Prepared Resources tree, packaged Node/Python executables, primary-runtime payload digests, package-set closure, builder configuration, target architecture, and install source.
seams.whyItMatters: A candidate is only installable if the staged runtime tree and its qualified payload closure still describe the current upstream layout.
seams.failureMode: An incomplete runtime, wrong architecture, missing native module, or unqualified update payload reaches a packaged artifact.
seams.detectionMethod: Path/rename detection plus package/build manifest, runtime-lock, and runtime-tree structural signals.

seams.description: Cordis patch schema and package-set loading that inject the DS Harness capability composition through the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-custom` tail patch. The historical `desktop-custom-composition` and `desktop-dev-composition` package-set implementation is retired; the seam ID is retained for report/state compatibility while its evidence points at the current tail-patch architecture.
seams.interface: Cordis patch declarations, package names/exports, built-in package resolution, generated catalogs, and Desktop package-set materialization.
seams.whyItMatters: The composition is how every DS Harness capability reaches the product runtime; a silent omission is invisible until runtime.
seams.failureMode: The tail patch references a removed package or duplicates a new upstream native service, and the Custom runtime fails or loads a partial capability set.
seams.detectionMethod: Bundle/package/loader path detection, manifest changes, patch-schema changes, and rename tracking.

seams.description: Client package export faces, remote client registration, slot ownership, and renderer package loading.
seams.interface: Client/remote export maps, package manifest loading, dockkit and scoped UI slots, connection commands, and renderer registration.
seams.whyItMatters: The DS Harness client half is only reachable through the current export, catalog, and slot conventions.
seams.failureMode: Old export or renderer entry assumptions leave the Custom client packages unmounted or mounted at the wrong slot.
seams.detectionMethod: Contract-path and package-export changes; exact rename detection for client contracts.

seams.description: Custom profile/flavor selection and the intentional isolation/sharing boundary for userData, settings, and Sessions.
seams.interface: Flavor/profile path and name, profile-link resolution, settings ownership, Session persistence location/schema, migration, and userData derivation.
seams.whyItMatters: This is the data-safety boundary between the official product and DS Harness; mistakes are destructive and irreversible for user data.
seams.failureMode: An unqualified launch uses the official profile or migrates shared stores under unreviewed assumptions.
seams.detectionMethod: Exact data-boundary paths, schema/type files, migrations, and renames always require manual review.

seams.description: Agent lifecycle, turn/step, request-attempt, stream, retry, cancellation, and tool event surfaces projected by Run State and policy.
seams.interface: Run/Attempt correlation, agent event payloads, LlmAttemptId, model-attempt lifecycle, tool completion facts, retry gates, and cancellation acknowledgement.
seams.whyItMatters: Run State, run policy, and task checkpoints all derive their facts from these events; the projection cannot invent correlation semantics.
seams.failureMode: The projection misinterprets or misses new events while appearing to work, silently corrupting Run and Task state.
seams.detectionMethod: Agent/core contract paths, event schema/type changes, direct overlap, and rename detection.

seams.description: LLM request, reasoning effort, streaming chunks, durable retry classification, token usage, and provider adapter contracts.
seams.interface: Request-level reasoning effort, stream chunks, usage/cache accounting, durable retry waterfall, error payloads, and provider defaults.
seams.whyItMatters: DS Harness adds exactly one policy layer over provider-owned retry; duplicating provider behavior would double-apply limits.
seams.failureMode: Old error/retry or reasoning adapters conflict with provider behavior, or the policy misreads new usage fields.
seams.detectionMethod: Type/adapter contract paths and package export changes; adjacent implementation is medium risk pending review.

seams.description: Session event durability, known event registration, projection replay, and persistence format used by Run and Task state.
seams.interface: Durable Session v3 event envelope, known-type catalog, JSONL format, static migrations, projection registration/replay, ignorable single-writer extension events, and atomic persistence.
seams.whyItMatters: Task and Run durable facts must be written through the current envelope rules or cross-version persistence becomes unsafe.
seams.failureMode: Custom envelopes are rejected, or an unregistered extension event corrupts replay for other readers.
seams.detectionMethod: Schema/type/event/persistence paths and migrations; direct overlap is explicitly recorded.

seams.description: Compaction executor, surface replacement, token meter, tool-result governance, and auxiliary reasoning isolation.
seams.interface: Pressure facts, compaction eligibility/execution, candidate-policy validation, atomic surface apply, tool-output references, context-overflow recovery, and the task-aware protection/audit contract.
seams.whyItMatters: Upstream owns the executor and thresholds; DS Harness only adds task-aware eligibility, so a duplicated engine would discard new upstream safety behavior.
seams.failureMode: Two compaction systems coexist, or the task-aware layer authorizes a scope upstream no longer supports.
seams.detectionMethod: Compaction/token-surface paths, schema/type changes, and direct overlap detection.

seams.description: Read-only diagnostics transport and UI source contract from Run State to Run Details, including the Stage 11 transient compaction diagnostics stream.
seams.interface: Typert Remote service publication, Gateway stream transport, Resource Registry seats, generated client contributions, dock/scoped slot ownership, and explicit Unknown/idle presentation.
seams.whyItMatters: Upstream owns the transport and resource seats; the Stage 11 controller and Run Details must consume them read-only rather than open a second authority.
seams.failureMode: The diagnostics stream stops resolving, a second Remote authority or polling loop is introduced, or the dock loses its insertion point.
seams.detectionMethod: Remote/client contract, resource-seat, and slot paths; exact overlaps and renames increase confidence.

seams.description: Electron/Node ABI and packaged native modules required by the Desktop Host.
seams.interface: Electron version, primary Node version/architecture, Python runtime, native N-API boundary, target platform, and node-pty/koffi/sharp closure.
seams.whyItMatters: A packaged candidate loads native modules only if the Electron/Node ABI and primary-runtime payload closure still match.
seams.failureMode: An unloadable native module or a runtime tree built for the wrong architecture ships inside a signed artifact.
seams.detectionMethod: Manifest/lock/runtime-lock changes are inspected for Electron, Node, target, and named native dependencies rather than treating every dependency change as high risk.
